name: MiniMax Music 3.0 AI Music Generator
tagline: Web front end that turns a text prompt plus lyrics into a finished song with vocals and backing instrumentation.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The product here is not the interface, it is the music model behind it: a trained system that renders singing voices, lyric timing, arrangement and mix in one pass. Nobody one-shots that in a coding session, and nobody trains a credible replacement on a personal budget or a personal music library. What an agent can build in an afternoon is the shell: a prompt box, a lyrics field, a job queue, a local library of generated tracks. That shell still calls somebody else's hosted model and still bills you per generation, so you have rebuilt the packaging and rented the actual value. Worth noting this domain looks like a third-party wrapper rather than the model vendor's own storefront, so check who is actually charging you and what license the output carries before you commit.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you type a style prompt and lyrics, fire the job at a hosted music generation API, and browse, replay and export the resulting tracks from your own library.
requirements: An API key with credits for a hosted music generation model, for example Replicate or a vendor API
Node 20 and a local disk for audio files
Willingness to pay per generation, since the model is the part you cannot self-host
whatYouLose: The model itself: vocal quality, lyric alignment and mix polish are not things you reproduce locally
Per-generation cost control, you now pay raw API rates instead of a bundled plan
Any commercial-use clarity the paid service claims to grant on its outputs
Stems, extend, remix and structure controls if the underlying API does not expose them
Someone else's queue and GPU capacity when a render takes three minutes and fails halfway
moatNotes: Music generation quality tracks training data and compute, both of which sit outside a weekend project. Licensing of the output is a separate moat that a self-hosted shell inherits none of.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the alternative is writing, performing, arranging and mixing a song, or paying someone who can. A per-month or per-credit fee for something that spits out a listenable full track in ninety seconds is easy math for a podcast intro, a game loop or a birthday joke. The interface is not why anyone pays, the render is, and the render is a rented capability. The only real decision is whether you buy it through a wrapper site or straight from whoever runs the model.
notes: The front end is one sitting; the singer is not. The moat is a trained music model plus the GPU fleet to serve it, and an output license you cannot grant yourself.
prompt:
Build a local single-user web app called "songbench" for generating songs from prompts and lyrics via a hosted music generation API. This is a personal front end, not a model: be explicit in the README that the actual generation is a paid third-party API call.

Stack, no alternatives:
- Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind. No auth, no accounts, no telemetry.
- SQLite via better-sqlite3 for track metadata. Audio files on local disk under ./data/audio.
- Replicate as the generation backend, called from server actions only. Token in .env as REPLICATE_API_TOKEN, model slug in .env as MUSIC_MODEL so it can be swapped without code changes.

Features in scope:
- New track form: style prompt (textarea), optional lyrics (textarea), duration selector, seed field.
- Submit creates a row with status queued, then a background route polls the Replicate prediction until it succeeds or fails, downloads the audio to ./data/audio, and updates status and duration.
- Library page: list tracks newest first with prompt snippet, status badge, duration, HTML5 audio player inline, download button, delete button that also removes the file.
- Detail page per track: full prompt and lyrics, player, waveform is out of scope, a "regenerate with same inputs" button that creates a new row.
- Prompt presets: a hardcoded list of eight style strings the user can click to fill the prompt field.
- Cost log: store the model slug and a manual cost estimate per generation from a COST_PER_RUN env var, show a running total on the library page.

Out of scope, do not build: stem separation, lyric-to-melody alignment editing, sharing links, cloud storage, mobile app, any attempt to run or train a model locally.

Deliver: working npm run dev, migrations run automatically on boot, .env.example with the three variables, and a README that states plainly which parts are yours and which part you are renting.
